headline: Pinned in camp by a gale
summary: On the trail back from his Wyoming hunt, Roosevelt and his party sit out a day of howling wind and rain squalls rather than risk the open prairie.

events.detail: Stays in camp all day because of a violent windstorm

tr_quotes.text: Furious hurricane blowing, with driving rain squalls. Afraid to venture on prairie so stayed in camp all day.

uncertain: Exact location of the camp is not given.

headline: Strayed horses and a mare in the mud
summary: Wet bedding, wandering horses and a team mare stuck in a mud hole cost Roosevelt's party the day; it takes two hours to haul her out, and she is too weak to travel.

events.detail: Searches until noon for strayed horses, then spends two hours freeing a mare from a mud hole

tr_quotes.text: Still rainy; beds pretty wet; horses had strayed; could not find them till noon; then one of the team was in a mud hole; worked two hours to get her out; she could hardly stand, so had to stay in camp.

headline: Out of meat, he shoots supper
summary: After two days without meat, Roosevelt takes his shotgun out from camp on the big sand and brings back three teal and two sharp-tailed grouse.

events.detail: Shoots three teal and two sharptail grouse for the camp pot

tr_quotes.text: Very windy, and a little rain; camped on the big sand; been out of meat for two days; went out with shot gun and killed three teal and two chickens.
3 duck 2 sharptail grouse.

headline: A fifty-mile moonlight ride
summary: Roosevelt drives to Muddy Creek, shooting a jackrabbit and two grouse along the way. Then he and Bill Merrifield ride all night under the moon, 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., covering fifty miles to the Chimney Butte ranch. He later recalled the hoofbeats and coyote cries of that ride in print.

events.detail: Kills a jackrabbit and two sharptail grouse with his rifle
Rides through the night with Merrifield to reach Chimney Butte

tr_quotes.text: Clear and cold; drove to the Muddy Creek; on the way killed a jack rabbit and two sharptail grouse with the rifle + then by moonlight M. + I rode in 50 miles to the ranche, between 9 p.m. + 6 a.m.

the hoof-beats of our horses rang out in steady rhythm through the silence of the night, otherwise unbroken save now and then by the wailing cry of a coyote. The rolling plains stretched out on all sides of us, shimmering in the clear moonlight.

references.title: Ranch Life and the Hunting Trail

headline: Home from Wyoming with a big bag
summary: Back at Chimney Butte from the Bighorn country, Roosevelt tallies a season's take of more than a hundred birds and small animals, plus three grizzly bears, six elk and seven deer.

events.detail: Back at his Little Missouri ranch after the Wyoming trip
Counts up the trip's bag: 3 grizzlies, 6 elk, 7 deer and 100-plus birds and small animals

headline: Facing down the Marquis's gunman
summary: At Elkhorn, Sewall and Dow tell Roosevelt of threats against him and his men, of lynchings while he was away, and of the Marquis de Morès's hired gunmen stopping in for a meal. As the story was later told, Roosevelt rode to E. C. Paddock's cabin, told him that if there was to be killing it could start now, and warned him off his men and his claim.

events.detail: Rides to Elkhorn to see Sewall and Dow
Learns of death threats and of lynchings during his absence
Goes to E. C. Paddock's cabin and warns him to keep away from his hands and his claim

tr_quotes.text: let the killing begin now

uncertain: The confrontation with Paddock comes from later recollections (Sewall, and Hagedorn's Roosevelt in the Bad Lands), not a record made at the time.

headline: Felling logs for the Elkhorn house

tr_quotes.text: Shot five sharptail grouse from trees with rifle for Breakfast. Went on to where Seawall and Dow are hewing logs for ranche house.
